final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Aurora Global Database failover automation stack — provisions the SSM Automation
  document (AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument), its execution role, the Route 53
  Application Recovery Controller control plane, the writer-endpoint secret, and the
  TriggerFailover Lambda that starts the automation. The Aurora Global Database itself
  is intentionally out of scope and is supplied at runtime as GlobalClusterIdentifier.
  Documented gaps: (1) AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule is omitted pending
  verification of its assertion/gating sub-properties; (2) the request asked for
  python3.13 — python3.12 is used because it is the approved runtime here and the
  handler code is compatible with both.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: aurora-global-failover
    Description: Logical application name used for resource naming, tagging and the SSM Parameter Store path.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z0-9-]{3,48}'
    ConstraintDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (3-48 characters).

  SecondaryRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-west-2
    Description: Region hosting the standby Aurora Global Database cluster and the standby ARC routing control.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid AWS region identifier, e.g. us-west-2.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Route 53 Application Recovery Controller control plane (created in-template)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ArcCluster:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::Cluster
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  ArcControlPanel:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::ControlPanel
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-control-panel'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-control-panel'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  PrimaryRoutingControl:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::Region}-routing-control'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      ControlPanelArn: !Ref ArcControlPanel

  SecondaryRoutingControl:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SecondaryRegion}-routing-control'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      ControlPanelArn: !Ref ArcControlPanel

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Writer endpoint secret — generated, never a plain-text credential
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AuroraWriterEndpointSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}/writer-endpoint'
      Description: Aurora Global Database writer endpoint metadata maintained by the failover automation.
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "admin", "writerEndpoint": "pending"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-writer-endpoint'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parameter Store — the automation reads ARC identifiers from here, never from
  # literals embedded in the Python.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PrimaryRoutingControlArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/primary-routing-control-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the routing control representing the primary region.
      Value: !Ref PrimaryRoutingControl
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-primary-routing-control-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  SecondaryRoutingControlArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/secondary-routing-control-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the routing control representing the secondary region.
      Value: !Ref SecondaryRoutingControl
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-secondary-routing-control-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  ArcClusterArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/cluster-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the Route 53 ARC cluster whose data-plane endpoints serve routing control state.
      Value: !Ref ArcCluster
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  ActiveRegionParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/active-region'
      Type: String
      Description: Marker recording which region currently holds the Aurora Global Database writer.
      Value: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-active-region'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM — SSM Automation execution role
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SSMAutomationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role assumed by the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation document.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: aurora-global-database-failover
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AuroraGlobalDatabaseOperations
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - rds:FailoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:SwitchoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:DescribeGlobalClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBInstances
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusterEndpoints
                  - rds:PromoteReadReplicaDBCluster
                  - rds:ListTagsForResource
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ArcControlPlaneRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:Describe*
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:List*
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ArcDataPlaneRoutingControls
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:GetRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:UpdateRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:UpdateRoutingControlStates
                  - route53-recovery-readiness:GetReadinessCheckStatus
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: WriterEndpointSecretAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:PutSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:UpdateSecret
                Resource: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret

              - Sid: FailoverParameterStoreAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetParameter
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                  - ssm:GetParametersByPath
                  - ssm:PutParameter
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:*:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${AppName}/*'

              - Sid: AutomationSelfManagement
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ExecuteScriptLogging
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-ssm-automation-role'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM — Lambda trigger role
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  TriggerFailoverLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the TriggerFailover Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: pass-automation-role
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PassAutomationRoleToSsm
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:PassedToService: ssm.amazonaws.com
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-trigger-failover-role'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # Kept as a standalone policy: it references the automation document ARN, and the
  # document references the automation role, so inlining it on the role would create
  # a role -> document -> role dependency cycle.
  TriggerFailoverAutomationPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: start-and-monitor-aurora-failover-automation
      Roles:
        - !Ref TriggerFailoverLambdaRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: StartThisAutomationDocumentOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ssm:StartAutomationExecution
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:automation-definition/${AuroraFailoverDocument}:*'
          - Sid: MonitorAutomationExecutions
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
              - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
              - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
              - ssm:StopAutomationExecution
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:automation-execution/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Automation document
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AuroraFailoverDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      UpdateMethod: NewVersion
      TargetType: /
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Fails over an Aurora Global Database to its standby region, flips the Route 53
          Application Recovery Controller routing controls atomically, and records the new
          writer endpoint in Secrets Manager.
        assumeRole: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
        parameters:
          PrimaryRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region that normally hosts the Aurora Global Database writer cluster.
            default: us-east-1
          SecondaryRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region hosting the standby Aurora Global Database cluster.
            default: !Ref SecondaryRegion
          GlobalClusterIdentifier:
            type: String
            description: Identifier of the Aurora Global Database to fail over. Supplied at execution time.
          SecretArn:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the Secrets Manager secret holding the writer endpoint metadata.
            default: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret
          ParameterPrefix:
            type: String
            description: Parameter Store path prefix holding the ARC identifiers used by this automation.
            default: !Sub '/${AppName}'
          HomeRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region holding the Parameter Store entries and the writer endpoint secret.
            default: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          ArcControlPlaneRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region of the Route 53 ARC control plane endpoint used to discover cluster data-plane endpoints.
            default: us-west-2
        outputs:
          - DetermineActiveRegion.activeRegion
          - PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterRegion
        mainSteps:
          - name: DetermineActiveRegion
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Resolve which region currently holds the writer by reading ARC routing control state.
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: determine_active_region
              InputPayload:
                PrimaryRegion: '{{ PrimaryRegion }}'
                SecondaryRegion: '{{ SecondaryRegion }}'
                ParameterPrefix: '{{ ParameterPrefix }}'
                HomeRegion: '{{ HomeRegion }}'
                ArcControlPlaneRegion: '{{ ArcControlPlaneRegion }}'
              Script: |
                import boto3


                def determine_active_region(events, context):
                    prefix = events['ParameterPrefix'].rstrip('/')
                    primary_region = events['PrimaryRegion']
                    secondary_region = events['SecondaryRegion']
                    home_region = events['HomeRegion']
                    control_plane_region = events['ArcControlPlaneRegion']

                    ssm = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=home_region)

                    def read(suffix):
                        return ssm.get_parameter(Name=prefix + suffix)['Parameter']['Value']

                    cluster_arn = read('/arc/cluster-arn')
                    controls = {
                        primary_region: read('/arc/primary-routing-control-arn'),
                        secondary_region: read('/arc/secondary-routing-control-arn'),
                    }

                    config = boto3.client(
                        'route53-recovery-control-config',
                        region_name=control_plane_region,
                    )
                    cluster = config.describe_cluster(ClusterArn=cluster_arn)['Cluster']
                    endpoints = cluster.get('ClusterEndpoints', [])
                    if not endpoints:
                        raise RuntimeError('ARC cluster exposes no data-plane endpoints: ' + cluster_arn)

                    states = {}
                    last_error = None
                    for endpoint in endpoints:
                        try:
                            data_plane = boto3.client(
                                'route53-recovery-cluster',
                                region_name=endpoint['Region'],
                                endpoint_url=endpoint['Endpoint'],
                            )
                            resolved = {}
                            for region, arn in controls.items():
                                response = data_plane.get_routing_control_state(RoutingControlArn=arn)
                                resolved[region] = response['RoutingControlState']
                            states = resolved
                            break
                        except Exception as error:  # try the next regional data-plane endpoint
                            last_error = error

                    if not states:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'Unable to read routing control state from any ARC cluster endpoint: %s' % last_error
                        )

                    on_regions = sorted([r for r, s in states.items() if s == 'On'])
                    if len(on_regions) == 1:
                        active_region = on_regions[0]
                    else:
                        # Ambiguous control state (both On or both Off): fall back to the recorded marker.
                        active_region = read('/arc/active-region')

                    if active_region not in controls:
                        raise RuntimeError('Recorded active region is not a known failover region: ' + active_region)

                    standby_region = secondary_region if active_region == primary_region else primary_region

                    print('routing control states: %s -> active %s, standby %s' % (states, active_region, standby_region))

                    return {
                        'activeRegion': active_region,
                        'standbyRegion': standby_region,
                        'activeRoutingControlArn': controls[active_region],
                        'standbyRoutingControlArn': controls[standby_region],
                        'arcClusterArn': cluster_arn,
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: activeRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.activeRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: standbyRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.standbyRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: activeRoutingControlArn
                Selector: $.Payload.activeRoutingControlArn
                Type: String
              - Name: standbyRoutingControlArn
                Selector: $.Payload.standbyRoutingControlArn
                Type: String
              - Name: arcClusterArn
                Selector: $.Payload.arcClusterArn
                Type: String

          - name: PerformGlobalClusterFailover
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Fail the Aurora Global Database over to the standby region and wait for the new writer.
            timeoutSeconds: 1800
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: perform_failover
              InputPayload:
                PrimaryRegion: '{{ PrimaryRegion }}'
                TargetRegion: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.standbyRegion }}'
                GlobalClusterIdentifier: '{{ GlobalClusterIdentifier }}'
              Script: |
                import time

                import boto3


                def perform_failover(events, context):
                    primary_region = events['PrimaryRegion']
                    target_region = events['TargetRegion']
                    global_cluster_id = events['GlobalClusterIdentifier']

                    rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=primary_region)

                    def members():
                        clusters = rds.describe_global_clusters(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id
                        )['GlobalClusters']
                        if not clusters:
                            raise RuntimeError('Global cluster not found: ' + global_cluster_id)
                        return clusters[0].get('GlobalClusterMembers', [])

                    target_arn = None
                    for member in members():
                        cluster_arn = member['DBClusterArn']
                        if cluster_arn.split(':')[3] == target_region:
                            target_arn = cluster_arn

                    if target_arn is None:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'No member of %s found in region %s' % (global_cluster_id, target_region)
                        )

                    try:
                        rds.failover_global_cluster(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id,
                            TargetDbClusterIdentifier=target_arn,
                        )
                        mode = 'failover'
                    except Exception as failover_error:
                        # Planned, zero-data-loss path when an unplanned failover is not available.
                        print('failover_global_cluster unavailable (%s); falling back to switchover' % failover_error)
                        rds.switchover_global_cluster(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id,
                            TargetDbClusterIdentifier=target_arn,
                        )
                        mode = 'switchover'

                    target_rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=target_region)
                    target_cluster_id = target_arn.split(':')[-1]
                    deadline = time.time() + 1500

                    while time.time() < deadline:
                        promoted = False
                        for member in members():
                            if member['DBClusterArn'] == target_arn and member.get('IsWriter'):
                                promoted = True

                        described = target_rds.describe_db_clusters(
                            DBClusterIdentifier=target_cluster_id
                        )['DBClusters'][0]
                        status = described.get('Status')

                        if promoted and status == 'available':
                            return {
                                'newWriterClusterArn': target_arn,
                                'newWriterRegion': target_region,
                                'failoverMode': mode,
                                'clusterStatus': status,
                            }

                        print('waiting for writer promotion: promoted=%s status=%s' % (promoted, status))
                        time.sleep(15)

                    raise RuntimeError('Timed out waiting for %s to become the available writer' % target_arn)
            outputs:
              - Name: newWriterClusterArn
                Selector: $.Payload.newWriterClusterArn
                Type: String
              - Name: newWriterRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.newWriterRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: failoverMode
                Selector: $.Payload.failoverMode
                Type: String

          - name: FlipRoutingControlsAndUpdateSecret
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Atomically flip the ARC routing controls and publish the new writer endpoint.
            timeoutSeconds: 900
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: flip_and_update
              InputPayload:
                ArcClusterArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.arcClusterArn }}'
                PreviousActiveRoutingControlArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.activeRoutingControlArn }}'
                NewActiveRoutingControlArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.standbyRoutingControlArn }}'
                NewWriterRegion: '{{ PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterRegion }}'
                NewWriterClusterArn: '{{ PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterClusterArn }}'
                SecretArn: '{{ SecretArn }}'
                ParameterPrefix: '{{ ParameterPrefix }}'
                HomeRegion: '{{ HomeRegion }}'
                ArcControlPlaneRegion: '{{ ArcControlPlaneRegion }}'
              Script: |
                import datetime
                import json

                import boto3


                def flip_and_update(events, context):
                    arc_cluster_arn = events['ArcClusterArn']
                    previous_control_arn = events['PreviousActiveRoutingControlArn']
                    new_control_arn = events['NewActiveRoutingControlArn']
                    new_writer_region = events['NewWriterRegion']
                    new_writer_cluster_arn = events['NewWriterClusterArn']
                    secret_arn = events['SecretArn']
                    prefix = events['ParameterPrefix'].rstrip('/')
                    home_region = events['HomeRegion']
                    control_plane_region = events['ArcControlPlaneRegion']

                    config = boto3.client(
                        'route53-recovery-control-config',
                        region_name=control_plane_region,
                    )
                    endpoints = config.describe_cluster(
                        ClusterArn=arc_cluster_arn
                    )['Cluster'].get('ClusterEndpoints', [])
                    if not endpoints:
                        raise RuntimeError('ARC cluster exposes no data-plane endpoints: ' + arc_cluster_arn)

                    # One batched call so ARC evaluates the whole On/Off transition atomically.
                    entries = [
                        {'RoutingControlArn': new_control_arn, 'RoutingControlState': 'On'},
                        {'RoutingControlArn': previous_control_arn, 'RoutingControlState': 'Off'},
                    ]

                    flipped = False
                    last_error = None
                    for endpoint in endpoints:
                        try:
                            data_plane = boto3.client(
                                'route53-recovery-cluster',
                                region_name=endpoint['Region'],
                                endpoint_url=endpoint['Endpoint'],
                            )
                            data_plane.update_routing_control_states(
                                UpdateRoutingControlStateEntries=entries
                            )
                            flipped = True
                            break
                        except Exception as error:  # try the next regional data-plane endpoint
                            last_error = error

                    if not flipped:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'Unable to update routing control states via any ARC endpoint: %s' % last_error
                        )

                    rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=new_writer_region)
                    new_cluster_id = new_writer_cluster_arn.split(':')[-1]

                    writer_endpoint = None
                    for endpoint in rds.describe_db_cluster_endpoints(
                        DBClusterIdentifier=new_cluster_id
                    ).get('DBClusterEndpoints', []):
                        if endpoint.get('EndpointType') == 'WRITER':
                            writer_endpoint = endpoint.get('Endpoint')

                    if not writer_endpoint:
                        writer_endpoint = rds.describe_db_clusters(
                            DBClusterIdentifier=new_cluster_id
                        )['DBClusters'][0].get('Endpoint')

                    if not writer_endpoint:
                        raise RuntimeError('Could not resolve a writer endpoint for ' + new_writer_cluster_arn)

                    secret_region = secret_arn.split(':')[3]
                    secrets = boto3.client('secretsmanager', region_name=secret_region)

                    current = secrets.get_secret_value(SecretId=secret_arn)
                    try:
                        payload = json.loads(current['SecretString'])
                        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
                            payload = {}
                    except (KeyError, ValueError):
                        payload = {}

                    # Merge endpoint metadata only; the generated password is carried through
                    # untouched and is never printed.
                    payload['writerEndpoint'] = writer_endpoint
                    payload['host'] = writer_endpoint
                    payload['region'] = new_writer_region
                    payload['clusterArn'] = new_writer_cluster_arn
                    payload['updatedAt'] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()

                    secrets.put_secret_value(SecretId=secret_arn, SecretString=json.dumps(payload))

                    ssm = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=home_region)
                    ssm.put_parameter(
                        Name=prefix + '/arc/active-region',
                        Value=new_writer_region,
                        Type='String',
                        Overwrite=True,
                    )

                    print('routing controls flipped to %s; writer endpoint published' % new_writer_region)

                    return {
                        'writerEndpoint': writer_endpoint,
                        'activeRegion': new_writer_region,
                        'routingControlsUpdated': 'true',
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: writerEndpoint
                Selector: $.Payload.writerEndpoint
                Type: String
              - Name: activeRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.activeRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: routingControlsUpdated
                Selector: $.Payload.routingControlsUpdated
                Type: String

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda trigger
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  TriggerFailoverLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/TriggerFailover
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-trigger-failover-logs'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  TriggerFailoverFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: TriggerFailover
      Description: Starts the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation execution.
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      # The request named python3.13; python3.12 is the approved runtime here and the
      # handler below is compatible with either.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 60
      Role: !GetAtt TriggerFailoverLambdaRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          DOCUMENT_NAME: !Ref AuroraFailoverDocument
          AUTOMATION_ROLE_ARN: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
          SECRET_ARN: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret
          PRIMARY_REGION: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          SECONDARY_REGION: !Ref SecondaryRegion
          PARAMETER_PREFIX: !Sub '/${AppName}'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Start the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation execution."""

          import hashlib
          import json
          import os

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          REGION = os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']
          SSM = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=REGION)

          # Idempotency bucket: repeated invocations for the same global cluster inside the
          # same five-minute window collapse onto one automation execution, while a genuine
          # later failover of the same cluster still gets a fresh token.
          IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300


          def _unwrap(event):
              """Accept a raw event, a JSON string, or an API Gateway style envelope."""
              if isinstance(event, str):
                  try:
                      event = json.loads(event)
                  except ValueError:
                      return {}
              if not isinstance(event, dict):
                  return {}
              body = event.get('body')
              if isinstance(body, dict):
                  return body
              if isinstance(body, str):
                  try:
                      parsed = json.loads(body)
                  except ValueError:
                      return event
                  if isinstance(parsed, dict):
                      return parsed
              return event


          def _client_token(document_name, global_cluster_id, context):
              window = int(getattr(context, 'get_remaining_time_in_millis', lambda: 0)() or 0)
              del window  # remaining time is not a stable bucket; use the request epoch instead
              import time

              bucket = int(time.time() // IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_SECONDS)
              material = '|'.join([document_name, global_cluster_id, str(bucket)])
              digest = hashlib.sha256(material.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
              return 'failover-' + digest[:24]


          def _response(status_code, payload):
              return {
                  'statusCode': status_code,
                  'headers': {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
                  'body': json.dumps(payload),
              }


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              payload = _unwrap(event)

              global_cluster_id = payload.get('GlobalClusterIdentifier') or payload.get('globalClusterIdentifier')
              if isinstance(global_cluster_id, str):
                  global_cluster_id = global_cluster_id.strip()

              if not global_cluster_id:
                  return _response(400, {
                      'error': "Missing required input 'GlobalClusterIdentifier'.",
                      'detail': 'The Aurora Global Database identifier must be supplied in the invocation event; '
                                'it is deliberately not defaulted.',
                  })

              document_name = os.environ['DOCUMENT_NAME']

              parameters = {
                  'GlobalClusterIdentifier': [global_cluster_id],
                  'PrimaryRegion': [payload.get('PrimaryRegion') or os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']],
                  'SecondaryRegion': [payload.get('SecondaryRegion') or os.environ['SECONDARY_REGION']],
                  'SecretArn': [os.environ['SECRET_ARN']],
                  'ParameterPrefix': [os.environ['PARAMETER_PREFIX']],
                  'HomeRegion': [os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']],
              }

              client_token = payload.get('ClientToken') or _client_token(document_name, global_cluster_id, context)

              try:
                  result = SSM.start_automation_execution(
                      DocumentName=document_name,
                      Parameters=parameters,
                      ClientToken=client_token,
                  )
              except ClientError as error:
                  code = error.response.get('Error', {}).get('Code', 'ClientError')
                  print('start_automation_execution failed: %s' % code)
                  status = 409 if code in ('IdempotentParameterMismatch', 'AutomationExecutionLimitExceeded') else 500
                  return _response(status, {
                      'error': code,
                      'message': error.response.get('Error', {}).get('Message', ''),
                      'globalClusterIdentifier': global_cluster_id,
                  })

              execution_id = result['AutomationExecutionId']
              print('started automation %s for %s' % (execution_id, global_cluster_id))

              return _response(202, {
                  'AutomationExecutionId': execution_id,
                  'DocumentName': document_name,
                  'GlobalClusterIdentifier': global_cluster_id,
                  'ClientToken': client_token,
                  'message': 'Failover automation started. Poll GetAutomationExecution for status.',
              })
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: TriggerFailover
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

Outputs:

  SSMDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation document.
    Value: !Ref AuroraFailoverDocument

  SSMAutomationRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role assumed by the SSM Automation document.
    Value: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn

  TriggerFailoverFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the TriggerFailover Lambda function that starts the automation.
    Value: !GetAtt TriggerFailoverFunction.Arn

  WriterEndpointSecretArn:
    Description: ARN of the Secrets Manager secret holding the current writer endpoint metadata.
    Value: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret

    Description: ARN of the Route 53 Application Recovery Controller cluster.
    Value: !Ref ArcCluster

  PrimaryRoutingControlArn:
    Description: ARN of the routing control representing the primary region.
    Value: !Ref PrimaryRoutingControl

  SecondaryRoutingControlArn:
    Description: ARN of the routing control representing the secondary region.
    Value: !Ref SecondaryRoutingControl

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Kinesis ingest stream (my-stream-kinesis) with an Amazon Cognito identity pool
  that grants UNAUTHENTICATED identities put-only access to the stream. Intended
  for TESTING ONLY.

# ==============================================================================
# SECURITY NOTICE - READ BEFORE DEPLOYING
# ==============================================================================
# This stack deliberately enables AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities on the Cognito
# identity pool and attaches an IAM role with kinesis:PutRecord / PutRecords to
# it. Any caller who obtains the identity pool ID (which is inherently a public
# value, typically embedded in client-side code) can mint temporary credentials
# anonymously and write arbitrary records into my-stream-kinesis. There is no
# authentication, no attribution, and no per-caller rate limiting.
#
# This is acceptable for the stated testing purpose ONLY. This stack MUST NOT be
# promoted to production without replacing the unauthenticated role with an
# authenticated identity provider (Cognito user pool, OIDC, or SAML) and moving
# the Kinesis write grant onto the authenticated role.
#
# DEPLOYMENT CAVEAT - STREAM NAME AND RETENTION POLICIES
# The Kinesis stream carries an explicit Name (my-stream-kinesis, as requested)
# together with DeletionPolicy: Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain. Deleting
# this stack therefore LEAVES the stream in the account, and a subsequent
# redeploy of this template into the same account and region will fail with a
# "Resource of type AWS::Kinesis::Stream with identifier my-stream-kinesis
# already exists" error. Either delete the orphaned stream manually before
# redeploying, or import it into the new stack.
# ==============================================================================

Resources:

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Kinesis data stream: 1 shard, provisioned mode, 24h retention (AWS minimum),
  # server-side encryption with the AWS-managed Kinesis key.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  KinesisStream:
    Type: AWS::Kinesis::Stream
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: my-stream-kinesis
      RetentionPeriodHours: 24
      StreamModeDetails:
        StreamMode: PROVISIONED
      ShardCount: 1
      StreamEncryption:
        EncryptionType: KMS
        # AWS-managed alias: account-agnostic, no customer KMS key required.
        KeyId: alias/aws/kinesis
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: my-stream-kinesis
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Cognito identity pool. No external identity providers are configured - a
  # greenfield account has no user pools or provider ARNs to reference.
  # The unauthenticated role is intentionally NOT set here; it is bound via the
  # separate IdentityPoolRoleAttachment below, because the role's trust policy
  # already Refs this pool and wiring it inline would be circular.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      # Identity pool names allow letters, digits, spaces and underscores only.
      IdentityPoolName: my_stream_kinesis_pool
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Role assumed by unauthenticated (guest) identities from the pool above.
  # Least privilege: put-only writes plus the minimum describe/list calls the
  # Kinesis SDKs need to resolve shards, all scoped to this one stream ARN.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CognitoUnauthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Grants unauthenticated Cognito identities put-only access to the
        my-stream-kinesis Kinesis stream. Testing use only.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCognitoUnauthenticatedWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: KinesisPutOnlyAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Write grant - put actions only. No GetRecords,
              # GetShardIterator, DeleteStream, MergeShards, SplitShard,
              # and no kinesis:* wildcard.
              - Sid: AllowPutToStream
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kinesis:PutRecord
                  - kinesis:PutRecords
                Resource: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
              # Read-only metadata needed by the AWS SDKs to bootstrap a
              # producer (shard discovery). Kept separate so the write grant
              # above stays minimal and auditable.
              - Sid: AllowStreamMetadataForProducerBootstrap
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kinesis:DescribeStreamSummary
                  - kinesis:ListShards
                Resource: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
      # No kms:GenerateDataKey / kms:Decrypt statement: the Kinesis service
      # handles encryption with the AWS-managed alias/aws/kinesis key on the
      # caller's behalf, and an AWS-managed key ARN cannot be resolved here.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: my-stream-kinesis-cognito-unauth
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Binds the unauthenticated role to the identity pool. Separate resource to
  # avoid the IdentityPool <-> Role circular dependency. RoleMappings is omitted
  # because no identity providers are configured.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IdentityPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref IdentityPool
      Roles:
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn

Outputs:

  IdentityPoolId:
    Description: >-
      ID of the Cognito identity pool that vends unauthenticated credentials for
      writing to my-stream-kinesis. Treat as public; it grants anonymous writes.
    Value: !Ref IdentityPool
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdentityPoolId'

  KinesisStreamName:
    Description: Name of the Kinesis data stream.
    Value: !Ref KinesisStream
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-KinesisStreamName'

  KinesisStreamArn:
    Description: ARN of the Kinesis data stream.
    Value: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-KinesisStreamArn'

  UnauthenticatedRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the IAM role assumed by unauthenticated identities. Useful for
      debugging CloudTrail events and permission failures.
    Value: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-UnauthenticatedRoleArn'

Description: >-
  Multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard on AWS App Runner with self-built ECR image.
  LIMITATION: this stack builds a placeholder container image. Tags are immutable.
  To deploy the real dashboard application, push it to this repository under a new

                  "tagStatus": "untagged",
                  "countType": "sinceImagePushed",

                "action": {
                  "type": "expire"
                }
              },
              {
                "rulePriority": 2,
                "description": "Keep only the 10 most recent images",
                "selection": {
                  "tagStatus": "any",

                  "countNumber": 10
                },
                "action": {
                  "type": "expire"

                  - ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
                  - ecr:InitiateLayerUpload
                  - ecr:UploadLayerPart
                  - ecr:CompleteLayerUpload
                  - ecr:PutImage
                  - ecr:DescribeImages
                Resource: !GetAtt EcrRepository.Arn

                  from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

                  class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

                          if self.path == '/status':

                          self.end_headers()
                          self.wfile.write(body)

      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StartAndPollImageBuild
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codebuild:StartBuild
                  - codebuild:BatchGetBuilds
                Resource: !GetAtt ImageBuildProject.Arn

  ImageBuildFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Custom resource that runs the CodeBuild image build with a unique tag and waits for completion.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Timeout: 900
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt ImageBuildFunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import time
          import uuid
          import boto3
          import cfnresponse


          def handler(event, context):
              data = {}
              physical_id = event.get('PhysicalResourceId', 'image-build')
              try:
                  if event['RequestType'] == 'Delete':
                      cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.SUCCESS, data, physical_id)
                      return
                  props = event['ResourceProperties']
                  version = str(props.get('BuildVersion', '1'))
                  image_tag = 'v' + version + '-' + time.strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S', time.gmtime()) + '-' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
                  image_uri = props['RepositoryUri'] + ':' + image_tag
                  data['ImageUri'] = image_uri
                  data['ImageTag'] = image_tag
                  physical_id = image_uri
                  codebuild = boto3.client('codebuild')
                  build_id = codebuild.start_build(
                      projectName=props['ProjectName'],
                      environmentVariablesOverride=[
                          {'name': 'IMAGE_TAG', 'value': image_tag, 'type': 'PLAINTEXT'}
                      ]
                  )['build']['id']
                  print('Started build ' + build_id + ' for ' + image_uri)
                  while True:
                      build = codebuild.batch_get_builds(ids=[build_id])['builds'][0]
                      status = build['buildStatus']
                      if status == 'SUCCEEDED':
                          cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.SUCCESS, data, physical_id)
                          return
                      if status != 'IN_PROGRESS':
                          cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.FAILED, data, physical_id,
                                           reason='Build ' + build_id + ' finished with status ' + status)
                          return
                      if context.get_remaining_time_in_millis() < 30000:
                          cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.FAILED, data, physical_id,
                                           reason='Timed out waiting for build ' + build_id)
                          return
                      time.sleep(15)
              except Exception as exc:
                  print('Error: ' + str(exc))
                  cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.FAILED, data, physical_id,
                                   reason=str(exc)[:250])

        - Key: Application
          Value: multi-tenant-quicksight-dashboard

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Creates six EventBridge cross-account forwarding IAM roles, one per event source (CloudWatch, CloudFormation, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Slack notifications, Auto Scaling), each scoped to publish only to its own central sink event bus.

# NOTE: The central sink event buses must have resource-based policies
# (AWS::Events::EventBusPolicy) in the central logging account that allow
# these role ARNs (or this source account) to call events:PutEvents.
# That is out of scope for this template because those policies are deployed
# separately in the central logging account.

Parameters:
  NamingPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: org-eventbridge
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be 1-32 characters of lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens.
    Description: Shared naming prefix applied to every forwarding role name.

  CentralLoggingAccountId:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^$|^[0-9]{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be empty or a 12-digit AWS account ID.
    Description: AWS account ID of the central logging account that hosts the sink event buses. Leave empty to target the current account.

Conditions:
  UseCurrentAccount: !Equals [!Ref CentralLoggingAccountId, '']

Mappings:
  EventSourceConfig:
    CloudWatch:
      RoleSuffix: cloudwatch-forwarder
      SinkBusName: cloudwatch-sink-bus
    CloudFormation:
      RoleSuffix: cloudformation-forwarder
      SinkBusName: cloudformation-sink-bus
    CloudTrail:
      RoleSuffix: cloudtrail-forwarder
      SinkBusName: cloudtrail-sink-bus
    GuardDuty:
      RoleSuffix: guardduty-forwarder
      SinkBusName: guardduty-sink-bus
    Slack:
      RoleSuffix: slack-forwarder
      SinkBusName: slack-notifications-sink-bus
    AutoScaling:
      RoleSuffix: autoscaling-forwarder
      SinkBusName: autoscaling-sink-bus

Resources:
  CloudWatchForwarderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub
        - '${NamingPrefix}-${Suffix}-role'
        - Suffix: !FindInMap [EventSourceConfig, CloudWatch, RoleSuffix]
      Path: /
      Description: !Sub
        - 'EventBridge forwarder role for CloudWatch events; publishes only to the ${SinkBusName} central sink bus'
        - SinkBusName: !FindInMap [EventSourceConfig, CloudWatch, SinkBusName]
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: events.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PutEventsToCentralSinkBus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !Sub
                  - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${TargetAccountId}:event-bus/${SinkBusName}'
                  - TargetAccountId: !If [UseCurrentAccount, !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', !Ref CentralLoggingAccountId]
                    SinkBusName: !FindInMap [EventSourceConfig, CloudWatch, SinkBusName]
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: centralized-event-forwarding
        - Key: Environment
          Value: production
        - Key: Owner
          Value: cloud-platform-team
        - Key: CostCenter
          Value: security-operations
        - Key: DataClassification
          Value: internal
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation
        - Key: EventSource
          Value: CloudWatch

                  - TargetAccountId: !If [UseCurrentAccount, !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', !Ref CentralLoggingAccountId]
                    SinkBusName: !FindInMap [EventSourceConfig, CloudFormation, SinkBusName]
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: centralized-event-forwarding
        - Key: Environment
          Value: production
        - Key: Owner
          Value: cloud-platform-team
        - Key: CostCenter
          Value: security-operations
        - Key: DataClassification
          Value: internal
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation
        - Key: EventSource
          Value: CloudFormation

    Properties:

            Statement:

                  - TargetAccountId: !If [UseCurrentAccount, !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', !Ref CentralLoggingAccountId]
                    SinkBusName: !FindInMap [EventSourceConfig, GuardDuty, SinkBusName]
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: centralized-event-forwarding
        - Key: Environment
          Value: production
        - Key: Owner
          Value: cloud-platform-team
        - Key: CostCenter
          Value: security-operations

Description: >-
  Custom SSM Automation remediation for CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark control 3.9
  "Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs" (renumbered in newer CIS
  versions; referenced here by name). Provides a KMS-encrypted CloudWatch Logs
  log group, a flow logs delivery role, an automation execution role, an
  Automation document that enables REJECT traffic flow logging on a VPC via a
  Python script, and a dependent Automation document that routes the same

Resources:

  FlowLogsLogGroup:

    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/cis/vpc-flow-logs/${AWS::StackName}'
      RetentionInDays: 365

    Properties:
      Description: Role assumed by VPC Flow Logs and SSM Automation to deliver flow logs to CloudWatch Logs and manage EC2 flow log resources.
      Path: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}-flowlogs/'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:

              - Sid: TagFlowLogsOnCreate

                Resource: !GetAtt FlowLogsDeliveryRole.Arn

    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EnableVpcFlowLogs-Reject'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      UpdateMethod: NewVersion
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Enables VPC flow logging capturing REJECT traffic to a KMS-encrypted
          CloudWatch Logs log group for the supplied VPC (CIS AWS Foundations
          Benchmark control 3.9 - Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs).
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: ID of the VPC on which to enable flow logging.
            allowedPattern: '^vpc-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the IAM role used to run this automation.
            default: !GetAtt AutomationExecutionRole.Arn
          FlowLogsRoleArn:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the IAM role that VPC Flow Logs uses to publish to CloudWatch Logs.
            default: !GetAtt FlowLogsDeliveryRole.Arn
          LogGroupName:
            type: String
            description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group receiving the flow log data.
            default: !Ref FlowLogsLogGroup
        mainSteps:
          - name: EnableRejectFlowLogs
            action: aws:executeScript
            onFailure: Abort
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                VpcId: '{{ VpcId }}'
                FlowLogsRoleArn: '{{ FlowLogsRoleArn }}'
                LogGroupName: '{{ LogGroupName }}'
              Script: |
                import boto3


                def handler(events, context):
                    vpc_id = events['VpcId']
                    role_arn = events['FlowLogsRoleArn']
                    log_group_name = events['LogGroupName']
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    ec2.describe_vpcs(VpcIds=[vpc_id])

                    existing = ec2.describe_flow_logs(
                        Filters=[{'Name': 'resource-id', 'Values': [vpc_id]}]
                    ).get('FlowLogs', [])
                    matching = [
                        fl['FlowLogId']
                        for fl in existing
                        if fl.get('TrafficType') in ('REJECT', 'ALL')
                        and fl.get('LogGroupName') == log_group_name
                        and fl.get('FlowLogStatus') == 'ACTIVE'
                    ]
                    if matching:
                        return {'FlowLogIds': matching, 'Created': False}

                    response = ec2.create_flow_logs(
                        ResourceIds=[vpc_id],
                        ResourceType='VPC',
                        TrafficType='REJECT',
                        LogDestinationType='cloud-watch-logs',
                        LogGroupName=log_group_name,
                        DeliverLogsPermissionArn=role_arn,
                        MaxAggregationInterval=60,
                        TagSpecifications=[
                            {
                                'ResourceType': 'vpc-flow-log',
                                'Tags': [
                                    {'Key': 'Compliance', 'Value': 'CIS-AWS-Foundations'},
                                    {'Key': 'Control', 'Value': 'VPC-FlowLogs'},
                                ],
                            }
                        ],
                    )
                    unsuccessful = response.get('Unsuccessful', [])
                    if unsuccessful:
                        raise RuntimeError('Failed to create flow log: ' + str(unsuccessful))
                    flow_log_ids = response.get('FlowLogIds', [])
                    if not flow_log_ids:
                        raise RuntimeError('CreateFlowLogs returned no flow log IDs for ' + vpc_id)
                    return {'FlowLogIds': flow_log_ids, 'Created': True}
            outputs:
              - Name: CreatedFlowLogIds
                Selector: $.Payload.FlowLogIds
                Type: StringList
          - name: VerifyFlowLogs
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            onFailure: Abort
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeFlowLogs
              Filter:
                - Name: resource-id
                  Values:
                    - '{{ VpcId }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: FlowLogIds
                Selector: $.FlowLogs..FlowLogId
                Type: StringList
        outputs:
          - VerifyFlowLogs.FlowLogIds
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: CIS-AWS-Foundations
        - Key: Control
          Value: VPC-FlowLogs
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

            default: AWS-HelloWorldChangeTemplate

              Api: StartChangeRequestExecution
              DocumentName: '{{ ChangeTemplateName }}'
              ChangeRequestName: '{{ ChangeRequestName }}'
              ChangeDetails: 'Enable VPC flow logs capturing REJECT traffic on {{ VpcId }} per CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark control 3.9 (VPC flow logging enabled in all VPCs).'
              Runbooks:

                      - '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'

                      - !GetAtt FlowLogsDeliveryRole.Arn

                      - !Ref FlowLogsLogGroup
            outputs:
              - Name: ChangeRequestExecutionId

          - name: WaitForChangeRequestCompletion

        outputs:
          - SubmitChangeRequest.ChangeRequestExecutionId
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance

          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

  ReusableDelegationSetFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref FunctionName
      Description: Manages a Route53 reusable delegation set for CloudFormation.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ReusableDelegationSetRole.Arn
      Timeout: 90
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import hashlib
          import json
          import logging
          import re
          import socket
          import boto3
          import cfnresponse
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          log = logging.getLogger()
          log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
          r53 = boto3.client('route53')
          VALID_ID = re.compile(r'^[A-Z0-9]{1,32}$')
          # Slot order by TLD: awsdns slot 1-4 -> .com, .net, .org, .co.uk
          SUFFIXES = ['.com', '.net', '.org', '.co.uk']
          # CloudFormation rejects exports with empty values, so a non-empty
          # placeholder is used instead of an empty string on lookup failure.
          PLACEHOLDER = 'UNRESOLVED'


          def resolve(host, family):
              if not host or host == PLACEHOLDER:
                  return PLACEHOLDER
              try:
                  infos = socket.getaddrinfo(host, None, family,
                                             socket.SOCK_STREAM)
                  if infos:
                      return infos[0][4][0]
                  log.warning('No address for %s (family %s)', host, family)
              except Exception as e:
                  log.warning('Lookup of %s (family %s) failed: %s',
                              host, family, e)
              return PLACEHOLDER


          def build(ds):
              ds_id = ds['Id'].replace('/delegationset/', '')
              servers = [s.lower().rstrip('.') for s in ds.get('NameServers', [])]
              slots = [''] * 4
              left = list(servers)
              for i, suf in enumerate(SUFFIXES):
                  match = next((s for s in left if s.endswith(suf)), '')
                  if match:
                      slots[i] = match
                      left.remove(match)
              left.sort()
              for i in range(4):
                  if not slots[i]:
                      if left:
                          slots[i] = left.pop(0)
                          log.warning('Slot %d filled by fallback with %s',
                                      i + 1, slots[i])
                      else:
                          slots[i] = PLACEHOLDER
                          log.warning('No nameserver for slot %d in %s',
                                      i + 1, servers)
              data = {'DelegationSetId': ds_id}
              for n in range(1, 5):
                  host = slots[n - 1]
                  data['NameServer%d' % n] = host
                  data['NameServer%dIPv4' % n] = resolve(host, socket.AF_INET)
                  data['NameServer%dIPv6' % n] = resolve(host, socket.AF_INET6)
              return ds_id, data


          def validate(data):
              if not data.get('DelegationSetId'):
                  raise ValueError('DelegationSetId missing from Route53 response')
              for n in range(1, 5):
                  for k in ('NameServer%d', 'NameServer%dIPv4',
                            'NameServer%dIPv6'):
                      key = k % n
                      if not isinstance(data.get(key), str) or not data[key]:
                          log.warning('Attribute %s empty; using placeholder', key)
                          data[key] = PLACEHOLDER


          def handler(event, context):
              log.info('Event: %s', json.dumps(event, default=str))
              status = cfnresponse.FAILED
              data = {}
              reason = None
              pid = event.get('PhysicalResourceId')
              try:
                  rt = event['RequestType']
                  if rt == 'Create':
                      raw = '%s|%s|%s' % (event['StackId'],
                                          event['LogicalResourceId'],
                                          event['RequestId'])
                      ref = hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()
                      resp = r53.create_reusable_delegation_set(CallerReference=ref)
                      pid, data = build(resp['DelegationSet'])
                      validate(data)
                  elif rt == 'Update':
                      # Delegation sets are immutable; keep the existing one.
                      resp = r53.get_reusable_delegation_set(Id=pid)
                      pid, data = build(resp['DelegationSet'])
                      validate(data)
                  elif rt == 'Delete':
                      if pid and VALID_ID.match(pid):
                          try:
                              r53.delete_reusable_delegation_set(Id=pid)
                              log.info('Deleted delegation set %s', pid)
                          except ClientError as e:
                              code = e.response['Error']['Code']
                              if code == 'NoSuchDelegationSet':
                                  log.info('Delegation set %s already gone', pid)
                              elif code == 'DelegationSetInUse':
                                  reason = ('Delegation set %s is still in use by '
                                            'hosted zones; detach or delete them '
                                            'first.' % pid)
                                  log.error(reason)
                                  raise
                              else:
                                  raise
                      else:
                          log.info('Physical ID %s is not a delegation set; '
                                   'nothing to delete', pid)
                  status = cfnresponse.SUCCESS
              except Exception as e:
                  log.exception('Request failed')
                  reason = reason or str(e)
              finally:
                  cfnresponse.send(event, context, status, data, pid,
                                   reason=reason)

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Creates a WebSocket API Gateway whose $default route asynchronously starts a
  STANDARD Step Functions workflow. The workflow waits 5 seconds and then sends
  a reply to the connected client through the API Gateway Management API.

Parameters:
  ApiStageName:
    Type: String
    Default: api
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Only letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens are allowed.
    Description: Name of the WebSocket API stage.

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # WebSocket API
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  WebSocketApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-websocket-api"
      ProtocolType: WEBSOCKET
      RouteSelectionExpression: "$request.body.action"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step Functions logging
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub "/aws/vendedlogs/states/${AWS::StackName}-statemachine"
      RetentionInDays: 30

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step Functions execution role
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ManageWebSocketConnections
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - execute-api:ManageConnections
                Resource: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:execute-api:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${WebSocketApi}/${ApiStageName}/POST/@connections/*"
        - PolicyName: StateMachineLogging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # CloudWatch Logs vended log delivery APIs do not support
              # resource-level permissions and require Resource "*".
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogDelivery
                  - logs:GetLogDelivery
                  - logs:UpdateLogDelivery
                  - logs:DeleteLogDelivery
                  - logs:ListLogDeliveries
                  - logs:PutResourcePolicy
                  - logs:DescribeResourcePolicies
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: "*"
        - PolicyName: StateMachineTracing
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # X-Ray trace APIs do not support resource-level permissions.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - xray:PutTraceSegments
                  - xray:PutTelemetryRecords
                  - xray:GetSamplingRules
                  - xray:GetSamplingTargets
                Resource: "*"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step Functions state machine
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-statemachine"
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: false
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt StateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      TracingConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
      DefinitionSubstitutions:
        ApiEndpoint: !Sub "${WebSocketApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}"
        ApiStage: !Ref ApiStageName
      Definition:
        Comment: Waits five seconds, then replies to the WebSocket client via the API Gateway Management API.
        StartAt: Wait
        States:
          Wait:
            Type: Wait
            Seconds: 5
            Next: SendResponse
          SendResponse:
            Type: Task
            Resource: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:states:::apigateway:invoke"
            Parameters:
              ApiEndpoint: "${ApiEndpoint}"
              Method: POST
              Stage: "${ApiStage}"
              Path.$: "States.Format('/@connections/{}', $.ConnectionID)"
              AuthType: IAM_ROLE
              RequestBody:
                message: "Processed by Step Functions after a 5 second wait."
                data.$: "$.data"
            Retry:
              - ErrorEquals:
                  - States.TaskFailed
                IntervalSeconds: 2
                MaxAttempts: 3
                BackoffRate: 2
            End: true

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # API Gateway role used to start Step Functions executions
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ApiGatewayStepFunctionsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: apigateway.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StartStateMachineExecution
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - states:StartExecution
                Resource: !Ref StateMachine

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Integration: WebSocket $default -> Step Functions StartExecution
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DefaultIntegration:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Integration
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      Description: Asynchronously starts a Step Functions execution for each incoming message.
      IntegrationType: AWS
      IntegrationMethod: POST
      IntegrationUri: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:states:action/StartExecution"
      CredentialsArn: !GetAtt ApiGatewayStepFunctionsRole.Arn
      PassthroughBehavior: NEVER
      TimeoutInMillis: 29000
      TemplateSelectionExpression: "\\$default"
      RequestTemplates:
        "$default": !Sub |
          {
            "input": "{\"data\": $util.escapeJavaScript($input.json('$')).replaceAll("\\'","'"), \"ConnectionID\": \"$context.connectionId\"}",
            "stateMachineArn": "${StateMachine}"
          }

  DefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      RouteKey: "$default"
      AuthorizationType: NONE
      OperationName: DefaultRoute
      Target: !Sub "integrations/${DefaultIntegration}"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Deployment and stage
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Deployment:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Deployment
    DependsOn:
      - DefaultRoute
    Properties:
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      Description: WebSocket API deployment

  # Stage access logging and execution logging are intentionally omitted:
  # WebSocket API logging requires an account-level API Gateway CloudWatch
  # role (AWS::ApiGateway::Account), which is an account-wide setting outside
  # the scope of this stack.
  Stage:
    Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Stage
    Properties:
      StageName: !Ref ApiStageName
      ApiId: !Ref WebSocketApi
      DeploymentId: !Ref Deployment
      Description: WebSocket API stage
      DefaultRouteSettings:
        ThrottlingBurstLimit: 100
        ThrottlingRateLimit: 50

Outputs:
  WebSocketApiId:
    Description: ID of the WebSocket API
    Value: !Ref WebSocketApi
  WebSocketURL:
    Description: WebSocket URL to connect clients to
    Value: !Sub "wss://${WebSocketApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}/${ApiStageName}"
  ConnectionsManagementURL:
    Description: API Gateway Management API endpoint for the stage
    Value: !Sub "https://${WebSocketApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}/${ApiStageName}/@connections"
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine
    Value: !Ref StateMachine
  StateMachineLogGroupName:
    Description: CloudWatch Logs log group for the state machine
    Value: !Ref StateMachineLogGroup
  ApiStage:
    Description: Deployed WebSocket API stage name
    Value: !Ref ApiStageName
